topics.title: COP31 reaches its final day
topics.summary: Climate delegates in Antalya are pushing to settle a final agreement as COP31 enters its closing hours, with finance and fossil-fuel language among the remaining points of debate.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a big group project reaches the deadline, are you the person who polishes every sentence, finds a compromise, or brings snacks for the exhausted team?

topics.title: AI jitters weigh on global markets
topics.summary: Asian shares headed for their weakest week since 2020 as investors reassessed high expectations around AI, while technology stocks remained under pressure.
topics.discussionPrompt: When everyone gets excited about the next big thing, do you jump in early, wait for the reviews, or quietly enjoy the old version that still works?

topics.title: Holiday shopping season approaches
topics.summary: Reuters says Black Friday sales and fresh economic data will give markets a new read on consumer confidence, as retailers enter the year-end shopping stretch.
topics.discussionPrompt: Are you a careful list-maker, an accidental last-minute shopper, or someone who treats browsing stores like a sport?

topics.title: Signal limits screenshots
topics.summary: Encrypted messaging service Signal said it will restrict screenshots to make it harder for AI agents to read private messages displayed on a screen.
topics.discussionPrompt: What tiny privacy setting do you wish more apps made easy to find: screenshot controls, simpler permissions, or a big old-fashioned off switch?

topics.title: Google picks Blue Origin for space computing
topics.summary: Google selected Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket for a planned 2029 launch of AI-computing satellites, linking the fast-growing AI sector with a new space project.
topics.discussionPrompt: If computers could work from space, what should they help with first: weather forecasts, maps, movies, or something nobody has invented yet?

topics.title: Voyager 1 reaches a new distance marker
topics.summary: NASA confirmed that Voyager 1 has reached a light-day from Earth, another milestone for the veteran spacecraft as it continues returning data from interstellar space.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you could send one cheerful message to a spacecraft already a light-day away, what would it say?

topics.title: Moon-soil potato experiment succeeds
topics.summary: Scientists reported growing potatoes in simulated lunar soil, a practical experiment that explores how future explorers might produce food away from Earth.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you had to grow one food on the Moon, would you choose potatoes, tomatoes, strawberries, or something wonderfully impractical?

topics.title: Webb finds ice around a young star
topics.summary: A new study using the James Webb Space Telescope found water and carbon-dioxide ice in the debris disk around Beta Pictoris, offering clues about planet-forming material.
topics.discussionPrompt: Does learning that ice exists around another star make space feel more familiar, more mysterious, or both at once?

topics.title: India space startup raises fresh funding
topics.summary: Indian satellite-data startup SatSure raised $7 million from a sovereign space fund, adding momentum to the country's expanding private space sector.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a satellite could give you one useful daily update, would you ask for weather, traffic, wildlife sightings, or the perfect stargazing forecast?

topics.title: OakNorth wins a U.S. banking licence
topics.summary: British digital bank OakNorth secured a U.S. banking charter, becoming the first foreign online lender to gain a broader licence as it expands in America.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would you trust a bank with no local branch if its app was excellent, or do you still like knowing there is a real front door somewhere?
